stem: A client with cancer-related fatigue says, 'I think I should stay in bed all day so I do not waste any energy.' Which response by the nurse is most appropriate?

options.A: Plan short rest periods and prioritize the activities that matter most, but balance rest with an individualized level of physical activity rather than remaining completely inactive.
options.B: Complete bed rest is the preferred fatigue-management strategy because physical activity reliably worsens cancer-related fatigue.
options.C: Ignore fatigue when planning the day and complete all usual activities at the same pace regardless of symptoms.
options.D: Avoid discussing activity with the healthcare team because fatigue-management strategies do not need to be individualized.

rationale: NCI recommends practical fatigue-management strategies that include choosing and prioritizing important activities, doing them when energy is highest, and using planned short rest periods. At the same time, exercise and physical activity can improve fatigue and physical functioning during and after cancer treatment, so complete inactivity is generally not the goal. Activity should be individualized to the client's condition, safety, treatment phase, and functional ability. Pushing through severe fatigue without pacing is also inappropriate because fatigue can interfere substantially with daily functioning and may have treatable contributors.
educational_objective: Teach balanced energy conservation for cancer-related fatigue by combining prioritization and short planned rest with individualized safe activity rather than complete inactivity or overexertion.
source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health

correction_summary: Upgraded the original energy-conservation item to correct a common false dichotomy between rest and activity. The final question preserves NCI-supported prioritization and planned rest but adds the equally important role of individualized physical activity, explicitly rejecting both complete inactivity and indiscriminate pushing through fatigue.
audit_findings: Original item was directionally correct but presented energy conservation mainly as rest/pacing without explicitly protecting against the misconception that complete inactivity is desirable.
Fresh NCI review supports prioritization and short rest periods and separately supports individualized exercise/physical activity for cancer-related fatigue.
The final answer balances rest and activity rather than prescribing a rigid universal exercise dose or bed-rest schedule.
The item remains distinct from Q1775, which tests recognition/assessment of cancer-related fatigue; Q1788 tests self-management and activity/rest teaching.
Independent adversarial review found one uniquely correct response with no ambiguity, second answer, cueing, unsupported exercise prescription, or unresolved source conflict.
